How to use the trade packs

The Revenue Recovery System works for any trade. These packs make it specific: the right reasons, the right seasons and the right objections for your work. Each pack contains:

  1. Missed-call text, tuned to the trade
  2. Quote angle: the one sentence that answers the trade's most common hesitation
  3. 12-month campaign calendar: what to send, and when
  4. Two seasonal campaigns, ready to send
  5. Maintenance plan example, with numbers to adjust
  6. Top 3 objections, with honest replies

Fill-ins are the same as the main system: {Business}, {You}, {First}, {Link}, {ReviewLink}, {Offer}.

Seasons: calendars assume a typical U.S. four-season climate. In the Sun Belt, shift cooling campaigns about a month earlier and shorten heating ones. In the Southern Hemisphere, flip them.

HVAC

Missed-call text

Hi, {You} with {Business}. Sorry I missed you, I'm on a call. Is your system not heating/cooling right now? Reply with what's happening and your zip and I'll get back to you fast. No heat or AC with kids or seniors at home? Reply URGENT.

Quote angle (replacement quotes):

"The price covers the equipment, the install to code, permits, haul-away of the old unit, and the {X}-year labor warranty, so you won't get surprise bills later."

12-month calendar

Month Campaign
Jan Heating check for anyone who skipped fall; maintenance plan push
Feb Indoor air quality (filters, humidifiers)
Mar Spring AC tune-up campaign (launch)
Apr AC tune-up reminder + plan offer
May Last call before summer; old-system replacement quotes follow-up
Jun Referral push (busy season, happy customers)
Jul Emergency-ready text: "here's what to check before you call"
Aug Replacement financing campaign for older systems
Sep Fall furnace tune-up campaign (launch)
Oct Furnace tune-up reminder + carbon monoxide safety
Nov Plan renewal / annual plan offer
Dec Thank-you + "before the holidays" heating check

Seasonal campaign 1: Spring AC tune-up - Text: "Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. AC season is around the corner, and a spring tune-up is the cheapest way to avoid a July breakdown. I have openings {weeks}. Want one?" - Email subject: "Before the first hot day" · Body: 3 sentences: most AC failures happen on the first heat wave; a tune-up checks refrigerant, electrical and drainage; reply with a day or book at {Link}.

Seasonal campaign 2: Fall furnace check - Text: "Hi {First}, it's {You} at {Business}. Before you turn the heat on for the season, we can do a safety check (burners, heat exchanger, CO). Openings {weeks}. Want me to save you a spot?" - Email subject: "Turn the heat on with confidence"

Maintenance plan example: Comfort Club: $17/month · spring AC + fall heating tune-up · priority service · 15% off repairs · no overtime fees.

Top objections 1. "It's still working, why tune it up?" → "Totally fair. Most tune-ups are about catching a $20 part before it takes out a $1,500 one. If it checks out fine, you've got peace of mind for summer." 2. "Another company quoted less." → "Could you check whether theirs includes the permit, haul-away and labor warranty? If it does and it's apples to apples, I'll tell you honestly whether I can match it." 3. "I need to think about the replacement." → "Of course. It's a big decision. Want me to send a repair-vs-replace comparison so you can see both numbers side by side?"

Missed-call text

This is {You} at {Business}, sorry I missed your call! If water is leaking right now, turn off the main shutoff (usually near the water heater or where the line enters the house) and reply URGENT. Otherwise reply with what's going on and I'll get back to you shortly.

Quote angle:

"This price is for doing it once and doing it right: the right materials, up to code, and guaranteed for {X}, so you're not calling someone back in six months."

Seasonal campaign 1: Water heater flush - Text: "Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. Water heaters usually need a flush once a year to clear sediment. It helps them last longer and heat faster. Want me to add yours to next week's route?" - Email subject: "The 30-minute job that adds years to your water heater"

Seasonal campaign 2: Holiday guest prep (November) - Text: "Hosting this holiday? Garbage disposals and guest toilets get the most clogs the day after. {Business} is doing quick drain checks this month. Want one before the guests arrive?" - Email subject: "Before the guests arrive"

Maintenance plan example: Home Plumbing Plan: $12/month · annual whole-home inspection + water heater flush · priority emergency response · 10% off repairs · no trip fee.

Top objections 1. "Can't you just patch it?" → "I can, and I'll quote both. The patch is ${x} and usually buys {time}; the fix is ${y} and is guaranteed. Your call." 2. "That's a lot for one hour." → "I get it. You're paying for the truck being stocked with the right parts, the license and the guarantee as well as the hour. If it's not fixed, you don't pay twice." 3. "I'll try fixing it myself first." → "Totally fine. Here's one tip that might save you a call: {tip}. If it doesn't work, I'm a text away."

House Cleaning

Missed-call text

Hi! This is {You} from {Business}. Sorry I missed your call. I'm with a client right now. Are you looking for a one-time clean or regular service? Reply with your zip and roughly how many bedrooms/bathrooms, and I'll send you a quote today.

Quote angle:

"Your price includes all supplies, the same trusted team each visit, and our re-clean guarantee: if anything's missed, we come back within 24 hours at no charge."

Jun Referral push + summer schedule
Jul Vacation prep / "come home to a clean house"

Seasonal campaign 1: Spring cleaning - Text: "Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. We're booking spring deep cleans now: baseboards, inside windows, behind the appliances. Want me to hold a date for you?" - Email subject: "Spring cleaning, without lifting a finger"

Seasonal campaign 2: Holiday reservation (October) - Text: "Hi {First}! Holiday cleaning dates fill up early. Want me to reserve one for the week before {holiday}? Just reply with a day." - Email subject: "Reserve your holiday clean"

Recurring plan example: Every-Other-Week Plan: recurring clean at {x}% off the one-time price · same team · priority holiday dates · skip or pause anytime.

Top objections 1. "Another service is cheaper." → "They might be! Worth asking whether they bring supplies, are insured, and come back if something's missed. If they do, great. If not, that's what the difference covers." 2. "I'm nervous about strangers in my house." → "Completely understandable. Our team is {background-checked / insured / the same people every time}, and you're welcome to be home for the first clean." 3. "I'll just do it myself." → "Fair! Most of our regulars started with one deep clean to get it to a baseline, then kept it up themselves. Want that option?"

Missed-call text

Hi, this is {You} with {Business}, sorry I missed your call. I'm probably behind a mower! Reply with your address or zip and what you need (mowing, cleanup, landscaping) and I'll send you a quote.

Quote angle:

"That's the full-season price: weekly visits, edging, blowing off hard surfaces, and we skip (and don't charge) weeks when the grass isn't growing."

Jul Drought/heat care tips + watering schedule
Aug Aeration & overseeding booking
Sep Aeration & overseeding

Seasonal campaign 1: Spring cleanup - Text: "Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. We're scheduling spring cleanups now: beds, leaves, first cut and edging. Want a spot in the first round?" - Email subject: "First-round spring cleanup spots"

Seasonal campaign 2: Fall cleanup - Text: "Hi {First}, leaf season! We're booking fall cleanups for {weeks}. Want me to add your yard to the schedule?" - Email subject: "Let us handle the leaves this year"

Season agreement example: Full-Season Plan: {n} visits March–November · fixed monthly price spread over 12 months · first priority for cleanups · 10% off add-ons.

Top objections 1. "The kid down the street does it for $30." → "He might do a great job! What you get with us is insurance, reliable weekly timing, and edging/cleanup every visit. If that matters, we're a good fit." 2. "Can I just do every other week?" → "Yes. Just know it costs a bit more per visit because the grass is longer, and it may look a little rough by day 12 in peak season." 3. "I'll wait until it gets bad." → "Totally your call. Our spring route fills up, though, so if you want a spot I'd reserve it now. You can cancel with no fee."

Electrical

Missed-call text

This is {You} with {Business}, sorry I missed you. If you see sparks, smell burning or have a panel that's hot to the touch, turn off the main breaker if it's safe and call 911 if there's fire. Otherwise reply with what's going on and I'll get right back to you.

Quote angle:

"The price includes the permit and inspection where required, so the work is on record. That matters for your insurance and when you sell the house."

Seasonal campaign 1: EV charger - Text: "Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. Thinking about an EV? We install home chargers, including the panel check to make sure your house can handle it. Want a free quote?" - Email subject: "Is your panel ready for an EV charger?"

Seasonal campaign 2: Smoke & CO detector check (September) - Text: "Hi {First}, quick safety reminder from {Business}. Smoke and CO detectors should be replaced every 10 years. We're doing whole-home detector checks this month. Want one?" - Email subject: "A 10-minute check that matters"

Maintenance plan example: Safe Home Plan: $10/month · annual electrical safety inspection · surge protector check · priority scheduling · 10% off repairs.

Top objections 1. "My brother-in-law can do it." → "Totally understand. Just know that unpermitted work can cause trouble with insurance claims and home sales. If you go that way, I'm happy to inspect it after." 2. "Why do I need a permit?" → "It means an inspector double-checks the work for safety. It protects you, and it's required for {job} in most areas." 3. "It's just one outlet." → "Small jobs are welcome! If you have a list of small things, we can do them all in one visit for one trip fee."

Missed-call text

Hi, {You} from {Business}. Sorry I missed your call! What are you seeing (ants, rodents, termites, bed bugs, something else)? Reply with a quick description and your zip and I'll get back to you today.

"This is a full treatment with a follow-up visit included. If they come back between treatments, so do we, at no charge."

Seasonal campaign 1: Spring perimeter - Text: "Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. Spring is when ants and spiders start moving in. A perimeter treatment now stops most of it before it starts. Want one scheduled?" - Email subject: "Stop spring pests before they start"

Seasonal campaign 2: Rodent prevention (October) - Text: "Hi {First}, mice start looking for warm spots this month. We do an exclusion check (sealing the gaps they use) as well as treatment. Want one before it gets cold?" - Email subject: "Keep the mice outside this winter"

Plan example: Quarterly Protection: $39/quarter (or $13/month) · 4 treatments/year · free re-treatments between visits · priority scheduling.

Top objections 1. "I'll buy spray at the hardware store." → "That can work for a few ants! Store sprays usually kill what you see but don't reach the colony, so they come back. If yours do, give me a text." 2. "Is it safe for my kids and pets?" → "Good question, and the right one to ask. We use {products} applied {where}, and I'll tell you exactly how long to keep pets off treated areas." 3. "Why quarterly?" → "Treatments break down over about three months. Quarterly keeps the barrier up all year, and re-treatments in between are free."
